 Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Yaxel Lendeborg, Draymond Green and Graham Ike will start Friday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 Podziemski is available after missing Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers due to a lower-back injury. His return means that De’Anthony Melton will come off the bench. Ike gets his first NBA start, letting Green play his usual power forward role. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Brandin Podziemski (back) is probable for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 Podziemski is trending in the right direction after he was initially listed as questionable with a back ailment. He missed Wednesday’s loss against the Lakers with the same injury. Now that he’s been upgraded to probable, Podziemski, who appeared in all 82 games last season, should start alongside Stephen Curry against the Grizzlies Friday.

 Brandin Podziemski (back) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 Podziemski did not play in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers, leading to De’Anthony Melton taking the starting spot. Melton played 21 minutes, while reserves Will Richard and Brandon Williams played 20 and 18 minutes, respectively. Expect a similar rotation if Podziemski can’t play on Friday.

 Warriors head coach Steve Kerr said on Wednesday that he’s hopeful Brandin Podziemski (back) will return for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 After missing practice on Monday, Podziemski will miss Wednesday’s opener against the Lakers due to lower back soreness. However, he may not be out long, with Kerr hoping Podz can play on Friday. De’Anthony Melton is the player whose role may expand the most while Podziemski sits.

 Podz missed practice on Monday and will now be unavailable for the season opener. There are high expectations for the type of impact he’ll make this season, so they’ll certainly miss him. De’Anthony Melton will likely replace him in the starting unit.

 Brandin Podziemski (back) did not participate in Monday’s practice. 
 This has been a bad 24 hours for the Warriors, who saw Stephen Curry suffer an ankle injury during Sunday’s open practice. Podziemski is dealing with a sore lower back, casting some doubt on his availability for Wednesday’s season opener against the Lakers. If he can’t play, De’Anthony Melton takes on added importance within the Warriors’ rotation. 
 Brandin Podziemski 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Brandin Podziemski contributed 17 points (6-of-12 FGs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers against the Lakers on Tuesday. 
 Podz signed a five-year extension with the Warriors just a few days ago, showing how important he is to their future. He has been solid so far during the preseason and should be an important piece for the Warriors once again this season. Following a rough start to last season, Podz closed the year out well and will look to carry some of that momentum into this season. 
 Brandin Podziemski 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Brandin Podziemski has agreed to a five-year, $110 million extension with the Warriors, reports ESPN’s Shams Charania. 
 The extension is fully guaranteed and includes a mutual option in the fifth year as well as a trade kicker, according to Charania. Podziemski is coming off his best season in the NBA where he played in all 82 games and set career-highs nearly across the board. He’s coming off the board in the ninth-round of fantasy drafts this year. 
 De'Anthony Melton 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #8 
 De’Anthony Melton (thumbs) told NBC Sports Bay Area that he expects to play both games of back-to-backs this season. 
 Focusing on honing one’s craft during the offseason, rather than rehabbing from an injury, can make a significant difference for a player. That was the case for Melton this offseason, despite procedures on both thumbs. Last summer was spent recovering from a torn ACL, while a back injury was the issue in the summer of 2024. A healthy Melton can be a factor in fantasy basketball, especially category leagues, whether he starts or comes off the bench. His injury history puts him in “late-round flier” territory in drafts, but Melton can still be a steal for managers. 
 Brandon Williams 
 GSW 
 Guard 
 #10 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Brandon Williams has agreed to a one-year, $2.6 million deal to join the Golden State Warriors. 
 In his third season with Dallas, Williams enjoyed the most productive campaign of his career behind averages of 13 points, 2.9 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 1.2 “stocks.” He’ll offer depth to a Warriors team that surprisingly stood pat during free agency, and Williams will compete for backup guard minutes with the likes of De’Anthony Melton and Will Richard.

 Amen Thompson had 20 points (9-of-15 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), 10 rebounds, four assists, two steals, two blocks and one three-pointer against the Spurs on Friday. 
 Thompson filled the stat sheet and had an excellent game for fantasy purposes against the Spurs. Houston is 2-0 heading into Saturday night’s road game against the Hawks.

 Darius Acuff puts up 33 points (10-of-26 FGs, 11-of-12 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, and two threes in 128-120 loss to the Blazers.
 The first thing you will see with Acuff is the points and get very excited. Then as you look at the rest of the stats, its pretty empty. He did get to the line 12 times and hit 11 which really should help your FT% category. While he did score a lot, especially in the second half when he got rolling, he will need to be better on the peripheral stats if he’s going to be a good category league player. He will have many more performances like this one later in the season.

 Collin Sexton finished Friday’s win over the Clippers with five points (2-of-6 FGs), one rebound, two assists, three steals and one three-pointer.
 Given the lack of on-ball playmakers on the Lakers’ bench, Sexton’s role could be an important one as he gets acclimated to his new team. While Luka Dončić or Austin Reaves was on the floor for every minute of Friday’s win, Sexton was asked to initiate the offense on some possessions. The numbers weren’t great, but the role may be one in which Sexton can offer late-round fantasy value in deep leagues. He isn’t a must-add, but placing him on watch lists, especially in deep leagues, wouldn’t be a bad idea.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Alperen Şengün had 29 points (10-of-20 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), seven rebounds, seven assists, one block and two three-pointers in Friday’s 114-110 victory over the Spurs. 
 Şengün was the player of the game in the win over the Spurs Friday. He played excellent defense, had a 29/7/7 line and had clutch baskets down the stretch. Considering he was going up against Victor Wembanyama for most of the game, it doesn’t get much better than this for Şengün. He’s off to a great start to the season after a down-year for him last season.

 Domantas Sabonis with a monster 27 points (10-of-13 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), nineteen rebounds, ten assists, a block and a three in 128-120 loss to the Blazers.
 An absolute crazy from Sabonis who looks to be a great fantasy player for the rest of the season. An underrated part of the offseason was the departure of DeMar DeRozan, who really impacted Sabonis and his production when he got to Sacramento. With him gone, Domantas will be in line for some great fantasy production and will likely have several more triple doubles this season.

 Ace Bailey scored six points (2-of-8 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, and a three in 21 minutes against the Pelicans.
 Ace ended up playing similar minutes and Jaxson Hayes ended up closing the game over him. Even though it wasn’t the most efficient night, what I liked most about tonight is how he crashed the glass and didn’t play selfishly. During the summer, he really put in the work and its starting show how much better he got over the summer. If you own Ace in dynasty leagues, you should be excited about what you’ve seen despite the bad shooting. He’s a better shooter than he showed today.
